findings.title: Contain line-listener throws in `createCollector`.

findings.body:
**Path-nested URLs keep their userinfo in `redactUrlUserinfo`.**

`independentTextUrls` treats a later hit as a separate URL only in one case. The hit must be outside the earlier URL's authority and query, and the character before it must be one of `"',;)>]}`. In every other case, the earlier URL absorbs the hit, and `redactUrlUserinfo` checks for `@` only inside the earlier URL's authority (`src/shared/urlRedact.ts:155-157`). Any credential in the nested URL then passes through unchanged.

How the leak happens, for `https://web.archive.org/web/2020/https://u:p@host/`:
- `discoverSchemes(run, true)` finds two hits.
- The `/` in the earlier path resets `inAuthority`, so the nested hit is outside the authority.
- The character before the nested hit is `/`, which is not in the delimiter list. The nested hit is dropped.
- `token` is `web.archive.org/web/2020/https://u:p@host/`. `authorityEnd` is 15, so `lastIndexOf('@', 14)` returns -1.
- The output is the input unchanged, and `u:p` stays visible.

A `=` separator gives the same result: `a=https://x.com/,b=https://u:p@y.com/` leaks `u:p`. `stripCredentialText` does not have this problem, because it processes every hit from `discoverSchemes`. Only the free-text display path leaks. It is the path used for narration and diagnostics.

The checks that matter are the `inAuthority` and `inQuery` guards. They keep a scheme inside a password or query value from counting as a separate URL. The delimiter requirement does not protect anything else. If you drop it, path-nested URLs get redacted, and the worst case is that some path text gets cut more than needed. Re-run the cases pinned in `test/config/url-redactor.test.ts` after the change.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    if (
-      independent.length === 0 ||
-      (!inAuthority && !inQuery && '\"\',;)>]}'.includes(run[hit.start - 1] ?? ''))
-    ) {
+    if (independent.length === 0 || (!inAuthority && !inQuery)) {
```
</details>
findings.title: Path-nested URLs keep their userinfo in `redactUrlUserinfo`.
